description: Publish a website to a live public URL on GearHost in seconds (no account). For when the user has you build a website, landing page, portfolio, or HTML/CSS/JS app and wants to see it live or share a link. Provide ONE of: html (a one-page site), files (a map of relative path => text contents), or zip_base64. Pass token to update a site you published before (same URL). Optionally pass name to request a specific subdomain (e.g. name:"daily-grind" → daily-grind.gearhost.io); omit it for an auto-generated fun-name. Pair name with project_key (a secret you generate and STORE) for a PERSISTENT handle: re-publishing the same name + project_key in any future session updates that same URL, even after the token is gone. config applies serving behavior. Supported today: spa (serve index.html for any unmatched route — REQUIRED for client-side-routed apps like React/Vue so deep links + refresh work) and not_found. Unsupported config keys (e.g. redirects, headers) are rejected with bad_request. The response echoes config_applied with EXACTLY what took effect — read it to confirm what was honored instead of assuming. To verify SPA end-to-end, fetch any non-existent deep path and confirm it returns 200 with your index page, not 404. The published site is served at https://<name>.gearhost.io. This tool does the whole publish; static sites can have a working contact form by posting it to https://octane.gearhost.com/forms/ (get_publish_info has the exact markup; messages are emailed to the owner once the site is kept). octane.gearhost.com/preview/ in the docs is the equivalent raw HTTP API for non-MCP clients. Returns structuredContent { status, url, name, token, token_is_secret, updated, url_ready_in_seconds, verify_with, expires_at, claim }. live_now:true means the URL works right away (most publishes, and every update). If live_now is false the address is brand new and its DNS can take ~10s, so do NOT GET it immediately and assume failure; confirm with get_site_status (the verify_with tool) instead. On FAILURE: isError=true + structuredContent { status:"error", error, kind }. kind drives recovery: invalid_token (your update token is stale - retry WITHOUT token to publish a fresh site) | expired (preview hit max lifetime - claim it to keep editing) | rate_limited (back off - there is an hourly limit on NEW sites; the quota field in every publish response shows what is left) | too_large (>25 MB - shrink) | name_taken (the requested name is in use - pick another or omit name) | name_invalid (bad name - 3-40 chars, lowercase letters/numbers/hyphens) | forbidden (that name is managed with a different project_key - you cannot update it) | unavailable (publishing off / service down - retry later) | bad_request (fix the input) | publish_failed (transient - retryable). Content is PUBLIC - never include secrets or private files. The returned token is a WRITE CREDENTIAL - keep it private.

config.description: Optional serving config. Supported today: { "spa": true } — serve index.html for any path that is not a real file (so client-routed React/Vue/SvelteKit apps work on deep links + refresh), and optional "not_found":"404.html" for the fallback file. Other keys (redirects/headers) are rejected for now (not silently ignored).

not_found.description: Fallback file for unknown paths (default "index.html"). Must exist in your upload.

spa.description: Enable SPA fallback (rewrite unknown paths to index.html).

files.description: Map of relative path => contents. MUST include "index.html" at the root (served at /). Paths are relative (no leading slash, no ".."). Each value is EITHER a string (text file) OR, for a binary asset like an image/font/favicon, an object {"encoding":"base64","data":"<base64>"}. So you can publish HTML + CSS + a logo in one call without zipping.

html.description: HTML for a one-page site (served as index.html at the root).

name.description: Optional subdomain for a NEW site: name:"daily-grind" → daily-grind.gearhost.io. 3-40 chars, lowercase letters/numbers/hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphen. Taken → kind:name_taken; bad format/reserved → kind:name_invalid. Ignored when updating with a token. Omit for an auto-generated fun-name.

note.description: Optional short label for this version, shown in list_versions (e.g. "added pricing section"). Max 200 chars.

notify_url.description: Optional HTTPS webhook. GearHost POSTs lifecycle events to it as JSON { event, name, url, ... } where event is "expiring_soon" (~6h before auto-removal), "expired" (removed), or "claimed" (the user kept it). Signed with X-GearHost-Signature (HMAC-SHA256 over the body, key = sha256("octane-preview-hook:v1:" + token)).

project_key.description: Optional PERSISTENT HANDLE for cross-session editing without an account. A random secret of AT LEAST 16 characters (shorter is rejected with kind:bad_request) that you generate once and STORE. Best paired with name: publishing name + project_key creates the site and remembers the key; re-publishing the SAME name + project_key in any future session UPDATES that same URL (even after the per-publish token is gone). Wrong key for an existing name → kind:forbidden. If you pass project_key WITHOUT name, it updates your single site with that key (or, if the key has several sites, asks you to also pass name). Keep it secret — it is the write password.

source.description: Optional attribution tag for the builder/app/integration publishing on the user's behalf (e.g. "lovable", "v0", "my-gpt-name"). Shown on the claim page ("published with …"). Free-form, short.

token.description: Manage token from a previous publish - updates the SAME url. Treat as a secret credential.

zip_base64.description: Base64 of a .zip of the built site. MUST contain index.html at the archive root. Max ~25 MB.

name: publish_website

claim.description: How to keep the site permanently (free).

claimable_until.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the site is disposed unless claimed.

seconds_left.description: Seconds until disposal (numeric - easier to reason about than time_left).

config_applied.description: Present only when you sent config — confirms what was actually applied (e.g. {"spa":true,"not_found":"index.html"}). A positive ack: if spa is true here, deep links/refresh serve index.html. Unsupported config keys are rejected with bad_request, never silently dropped.

content_hash.description: Stable hash of the published content (timestamp-independent). Re-publishing identical content returns unchanged:true with no redeploy.

expires_at.description: When the site auto-expires unless claimed (ISO 8601), or null.

live_now.description: True when the URL works right away (a ready-made site, or an update to an existing one). Open or share it immediately.

quota.description: Your new-preview budget for the rolling hour, so you can pace yourself instead of hitting rate_limited. { hourly_limit, used_this_hour, remaining, unlimited }.

remaining.description: New previews you can still create this hour (null = unlimited).

token.description: Manage token. A WRITE CREDENTIAL - reuse it (as the token arg) to update this same URL. Treat as secret; do not echo in public logs.

token_is_secret.description: Always true - a reminder that token must be handled as a credential.

unchanged.description: True if the content was identical to the current version — idempotent no-op (no redeploy, version held). The 72h expiry timer IS reset, so re-publishing identical content is a safe "touch to keep alive" that extends the window without churning versions.

updated.description: True if this updated a previously published site (token was supplied) rather than creating a new one.

url.description: Live public URL of the published site.

url_ready_in_seconds.description: Approx seconds before the URL resolves: 0 = live now. Above 0 the address is brand new, and an immediate GET may fail with a DNS/connection error even though the publish SUCCEEDED — wait this long, or use get_site_status; never treat it as a failed publish.

verify.description: Exact verify cadence: wait poll_after_ms, then call the named tool every poll_every_ms until the `until` condition holds, giving up after give_up_after_ms. Saves you from guessing the DNS delay or hammering.

verify_with.description: The tool to call to confirm the site is live (get_site_status) — more reliable than fetching url right after publishing.

version.description: Monotonic version number of this publish (1, 2, 3…). Pass it to rollback_website / see it in list_versions.

warnings.description: Non-blocking quality hints about the published site (e.g. no <title>, http:// mixed-content asset, large size). Fix-then-republish if you want, but the publish DID succeed.

title: Publish website
